claims.text: OC226A enhances the per-transaction limit for On-Device Biometric Authentication in UPI from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000 effective 07th August 2026.

OC226 initially introduced the On-Device biometric authentication facility with a per-transaction limit of Rs. 5,000 and stated that this limit would be reviewed in due course based on performance and evaluation.
OC226A states that all existing validations, compliance requirements, specifications, and regulatory guidelines shall continue to remain fully applicable after the limit enhancement.

OC226 requires UPI Applications / PSP Banks and Issuer Banks to ensure explicit customer consent is obtained with customers having the ability to opt out at any time for the additional authentication methods.
OC226 mandates that a fresh consent be obtained after each device binding operation before allowing further transactions.
OC226 requires Issuer Banks to disable the biometric method for all UPI Applications in case of changes or resets to the UPI PIN, declining transactions until a fresh consent is captured.
OC226 requires UPI Applications / PSP Banks to ensure key rotation operation is undertaken before one year of biometric enablement.

OC226 requires UPI Applications / PSP Banks to mark the customer as inactive for this method if no transactions are performed within ninety days through this method, activating only upon customer confirmation.
